summary: Chögyam Trungpa (1939–1987) worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied at St Antony's College, Oxford, and under teachers including Khenpo Gangshar and Jamgon Kongtrul of Sechen. He founded Naropa University, Shambhala International, and Kagyu Samye Ling.
Chönyi Drolma works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Thinley Norbu Rinpoche, Lama Tharchin Rinpoche, and Ngawang Zangpo (all attested 2011).

Clare Carlisle is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (circa 1995–2002). She served as Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Liverpool from circa 2006 to 2011.

Claude Jacques (1929–2018) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, studying under George Cœdès. He served as director at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (circa 1964–1973) and taught epigraphy and history at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 2017).
Claudia Weber is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit and Gregor Ahn.

Claudius Buchanan (1766–1815) worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Glasgow and Queens' College, Cambridge, and was appointed Vice-Provost at Fort William College in 1801.

Claus Oetke (1947–2019) was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Hamburg. He served as a wissenschaftlicher Assistent at the University of Hamburg (circa 1977–1988) and held a post at Stockholm University (circa 1990–2012).

Claus Vogel (1933–2012) was a scholar in Indology and Tibetology. He held posts at the University of Göttingen (circa 1964–1967) and University of Marburg (circa 1967–1976), and became a professor at the University of Bonn in 1976.

Colette Caillat (1921–2007) worked in Indology and linguistics. She served as Director at the University of Paris (circa 1969–1989) and was a member of the Institut de France and Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (circa 1987–2007).

Colette Sciberras works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She studied at Durham University under doctoral supervisors David E. Cooper and Simon P. James, as well as under traditional teachers Yungdrung Nyima and Chamtrul Rinpoche.
Colin Leslie Dean is a scholar in philosophy and Indology who studied under supervisors Peter Fenner and Purushottama Bilimoria (both attested 2002).

Collett Cox is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned a PhD at Columbia University and studied at the University of Tokyo and Ryukoku University. She served as a professor at the University of Washington (attested 1999, 2017).
Conor Roddy is a philosopher who completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2011), studying under Arindam Chakrabarti and Roger T. Ames.

Constance E. Kassor works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed a BA at Smith College and a PhD at Emory University, studying under John D. Dunne and Sara L. McClintock; she held a faculty post at Smith College (attested 2014).

Constance Powell Chin is a scholar in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. She earned a master's degree at San Jose State University by 2012, studying under MA supervisor John W. Bernhardt and teacher Christian Luczanits.

Constantin Regamey (1907–1982) studied Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies at the universities of Warsaw and Paris. He held a post at the University of Warsaw (circa 1936–1939) and professorships at the universities of Lausanne and Fribourg (circa 1945/1946–1977).
Cornelis Jan Kuiken is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Groningen by 2002, studying under Jaap den Hollander, Timothy H. Barrett, and Jan N. Bremmer.

Cornelis Petrus Tiele (1830–1902) was a scholar of religious studies and history and archaeology who studied at the University of Amsterdam (circa 1848–1853). He served as Professor of the History of Religions at Leiden University from circa 1877 to 1900.

Corrado Pensa works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, having studied under Giuseppe Tucci and Raniero Gnoli. He served as Professor of Religions and Philosophy of India and the Far East at Sapienza University of Rome (attested 1971).
Craig J. Reynolds is a historian and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Amherst College and Cornell University. He held a post at the Australian National University from circa 1989 to 2016.
